messages:
Maya: Quick sync — proposing an enterprise "spike safety net" to handle customers that burst past committed capacity. Three primary levers: auto overage credits (short-lived), soft throttles with warnings, and prioritized routing to Dedicated if purchased. Need clear launch criteria and fraud/abuse rules. @Sam @David @Leah
Sam: Prefer credit-first. Small pre-funded credit pool that auto-applies for a 24h grace window, then either bill or trigger throttles. UX should be one-click for finance teams.
David: Credits are fine but we need hard caps to avoid runaway costs. Cap by percentage of monthly commit and apply rules for repeated spikes (e.g., consecutive-day limits).
Leah: Do we have the telemetry to reliably separate a genuine spike from a bot/attack or a slow growth trend? We need metric definitions and a false-positive budget before we roll.
Maya: Proposed detection heuristics: 1) peak QPS > 3x baseline for >=2h; 2) sustained token rate > committed rate for >4h; 3) request signature patterns matching abuse. Product + SRE to validate.
product-bot: Draft policy example:
```
overage_guardrail:
  grace_window_hours: 24
  credit_pool_pct_of_commit: 5
  max_credit_per_month_usd: 50000
  auto_throttle_threshold_pct: 200
  throttle_profile: soft
  throttle_ramp_minutes: 30
  escalation: [notify_customer, notify_ops, contact_se]
```
Anna: Finance: if credits are pre-billed we need refund rules, lookback windows for repeat spikes, and GL mapping for deferred revenue. Also define how credits show up on invoices.
Sam: Pilot suggestion: run with 3 customers across different segments (SMB, mid, enterprise) for 6-8 weeks. During pilot, any auto-credit application requires manual ops review.
David: SLA guardrail — throttles must not violate latency SLAs. Prefer queue-admission throttles (reject or delay admission) over token-gen slowdowns. Ops will run sims.
Leah: Console UX: surface a prioritized banner and a one-click decision: "Apply credit / Start throttle / Escalate to SE". Ops and account teams must have an override path.
Maya: Launch criteria draft:
- telemetry coverage >= 95% for pilot customers
- pilot executed with 3 customers, <=2 manual escalations per customer
- legal signoff on overage terms and T&Cs
- finance approves accounting treatment and SKU mapping
If green, opt-in soft launch to customers who accept early access terms.
David: Add a monthly budget cap for auto credits per customer: max(fixed_$X, credit_pool_pct * commit). Need to pick $X by segment.
Anna: Proposed rollout tiers: Pilot (manual ops review), Early access (auto credits with 5% commit cap), GA (auto credits + purchasable overage addon SKUs). Map SKUs and meter names.
Sam: Suggest adding a protected API header for priority routing to Dedicated — simplifies routing rules. Must require entitlement check to avoid spoofing.
Leah: Agree, require signed entitlement token + server-side validation. Also add signal to detect header abuse.
Maya: Ops/Engineering action items:
- Sam: prototype credit UX + pilot onboarding flow by EOD Friday
- David + Ops: run throttle impact sims and report by Tuesday
- Leah: write detection rule set and Console flows by next Thursday (include FP targets; aim FPR <1% for pilot)
- Anna: draft accounting entries and SKU mapping for pilot/GA
- Legal: begin T&C phrasing and overage clauses (Maya will ping)
Sam: I'll mock the banner and the "Apply credit" modal; will include confirmation text with refund rules.
Leah: I'll build a small evaluation harness to surface false positives during pilot and log decisions.
Maya: Thanks — we'll reconvene after the sims. Marking for follow-up next Wednesday. :thumbsup:
